acceptance_signals: The first visible proposal-review content is a concise human-facing summary that states what approval does now, the task goal, future allowed scope, validation count, material risks or unknowns, and the authority boundary before any raw JSON.
The exact task-admission plan remains present after a clearly labeled secondary technical-details section for audit.
Decision labels directly distinguish approving only this task, sending it back for changes, and not approving it.
Approving still creates only the exact task record and does not start implementation or authorize scope expansion, Git, release, deployment, or publication.
Request changes, reject, decline, cancel, malformed input, stale inventory, and unsupported elicitation remain zero-write and fail closed.
Focused MCP tests protect summary-before-JSON ordering, required summary facts, exact technical detail retention, decision values, and unchanged authority behavior.
The first execution action after task take-up captures the exact task-start baseline before any repository write, and final comparison reports zero failures.
All pre-existing task records and unrelated dirty-worktree paths remain byte-identical to their task-start identities.
Affected current-state, admission, Adapter, product-requirement, ADR, and dated development-log documents describe the new summary-first behavior and its host-rendering limit.
The focused governance tests, documentation tests, complete Python 3.11 suite, task governance, repository governance, baseline comparison, privacy scan, and diff check pass.

decision.rationale: The accountable human reviewed structured proposal prp-ba72562c52084fdda9716ec7fef4e160 and admitted that exact task through an explicit admission control.

requirement.summary: Replace the JSON-first native task-admission message with a concise summary-first decision card, followed by clearly secondary exact technical details, while preserving the existing human authority and fail-closed contract.

items: The host owns final form chrome and may not support collapsible content; this task guarantees summary-first ordering, not a host-specific collapse control.
The worktree already contains unrelated changes, so the task-start baseline and explicit identity preservation are required before implementation.
The scope schema limit requires several pre-existing paths to be classified inside broad source and test prefixes; acceptance forbids modifying unrelated files under those prefixes.
Reviewed assumption: The current Codex form renders the elicitation message in order before the decision controls.
Reviewed assumption: Plain headings and bullets are more understandable than leading with the raw admission-plan JSON.
Reviewed assumption: English decision copy remains the portable default for all MCP hosts.
Reviewed unknown: Whether every supported host renders Markdown headings identically.
Reviewed unknown: Whether a future MCP or Codex host version will provide native collapsible technical-detail controls.

title: Native task-admission summary-first decision card v1
